ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: SAMR & PBOC Order No. 3 (2024) 'Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information Filing of Market Entities', effective November 1, 2024; PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (2006, as amended 2016); PRC Company Law (as amended 2018); PBOC 'Measures for the Identification and Management of Beneficial Owners in Financial Institutions' (PBOC Order [2018] No. 1); and the identity verification provisions of the PRC Civil Code.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investor's home jurisdiction company registry (e.g., Companies House, ACRA, Secretary of State)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If issuing jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member: notarize where required, then obtain an Apostille from the competent national authority; do NOT obtain consular legalization. If issuing jurisdiction is not a member: notarize, authenticate through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the PRC Embassy or Consulate. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Active Status) of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention states: Apostille issued by the designated competent authority after any required notarization; no consular legalization. For non-member states: notarization, then authentication by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalization by the PRC diplomatic mission. Never chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing formation of the WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or shareholders' meeting of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The resolution must be signed and notarized by a local notary public. If the jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state, the notarized resolution receives an Apostille from the competent authority. In non-member states, the notarized resolution is legalized via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then the PRC Embassy or Consulate. These are alternative pathways.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or equivalent constitutional instrument) of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investor's home registry, notary, or corporate counsel as certified copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy is notarized; Apostille path if Convention state (Apostille by competent authority). Non-Convention state: notarization, Foreign Ministry authentication, PRC consular legalization. Both paths yield uniform acceptance; they must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investor's commercial bank (with officer signature and bank seal)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter must be notarized at the branch or by a local notary, then Apostilled (Convention state) or legalized through the Foreign Ministry and PRC Consulate (non-Convention state). The bank's signature and seal must be verified before authentication.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, senior managers and authorized signatories of the WFOE must be screened against PEP databases maintained by the CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and domestic PRC anti-money laundering watchlists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons, their family members, close associates, and persons from FATF high-risk jurisdictions. Screening must be completed before incorporation, repeated at bank account opening, and updated continuously via automated 24/7 name-matching systems. Any positive hit requires escalation to the head of compliance and, where necessary, to the People's Bank of China and SAMR.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS, www.gsxt.gov.cn) operated by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), together with the local SAMR online pre-registration portal for enterprise name clearance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Chinese WFOE name must follow the statutory four-tier structure: administrative division + distinctive name + industry / business characteristic + company type. The distinctive name must be in standardized Chinese characters (Hanzi) and may not contain numerals, letters, Japanese kanji, or non-standard transliterations unless expressly approved. Foreign names must be transliterated into Chinese according to Hanyu Pinyin or established trade-name pronunciation, and the Chinese name is the authoritative legal name. Pinyin-only or English-only names are not registrable as the primary name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 business days after receiving a rejection notice, the applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration petition with the SAMR or with the local administrative department for market regulation that rendered the decision. The petition must restate the proposed name, enclose the rejection notice, and set out the legal and factual grounds for reversal, including evidence that the name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name. If the reconsideration body fails to issue a decision within 30 days, the applicant may treat the application as rejected and may bring an administrative lawsuit before the competent people's court within six months.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an AI/LLM API platform WFOE, a purely virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the registered address. PRC Company Law, local registration rules, and tax registration guidelines require a tangible, physically accessible premises for the business license, for tax inspection, and for payroll and administrative substance. Banks unequivocally reject virtual office addresses when opening a basic deposit account. A serviced or subleased office, supported by a valid lease, a copy of the property ownership certificate, and landlord consent, satisfies the requirement; a P.O. box or virtual address engine does not.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) visible door signage matching the registered name; (2) employees present during normal business hours; (3) IT equipment and office furniture appropriate for a software/AI development company; (4) original lease agreement, property ownership certificate, and rental invoices available on site; (5) business license photocopy displayed at the registered office; (6) evidence of actual operational management (meeting logs, admin personnel). Quantified risk: 75% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the municipal Administration for Market Regulation and the State Taxation Administration within the first 12 months of incorporation, heightened for technology companies accepting cryptocurrency.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fee schedules of the issuing country plus courier and service fees.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), particularly Articles 4, 10, 24, 25, 26, 27, 30, 32, 33, 34, 36, 37, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 67, 68, 74, 75, 83, 84, 90, 91 and 92; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020), Articles 2, 3, 4, 18, 22, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32 and 34; Regulations for the Implementation of the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020); Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746, effective 1 March 2022), Articles 2, 3, 5, 8, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22 and 26.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration with jurisdiction over the registered office; filings are made electronically through the national Enterprise Registration One-Window Online Service Platform and the SAMR integrated enterprise registration system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Filing Application Form and Articles of Association; the certificate of incorporation is the Unified Social Credit Code Business License.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital applies to a wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) limited liability company under Chinese law. The shareholders must determine a reasonable registered capital in the Articles of Association. Under Article 47 of the 2023 Company Law, each shareholder must contribute subscribed capital in full within five years from incorporation unless the Articles of Association specify a shorter period. No government-controlled blocked escrow account is required. The registered capital must be remitted into a designated foreign exchange capital account opened with a bank authorized by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), and all inward remittances will be subject to foreign exchange receipt verification procedures. For this Generative AI and LLM API platform, the registered capital should be sufficient to cover office lease, staff wages, computing infrastructure, cloud hosting, legal compliance, and working capital requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CN_WFOE_LTD (THE COMPANY), A WHOLLY FOREIGN-OWNED LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY ORGANIZED UNDER THE LAWS OF THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF CHINA. THIS RESOLUTION WAS DULY ADOPTED AT A MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS HELD AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE ON 15 SEPTEMBER 2025 AT 10:00 A.M. ALL DIRECTORS WERE PRESENT AND CONSTITUTED A QUORUM. ALL DIRECTORS VOLUNTARILY WAIVED FORMAL NOTICE IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION. WHEREAS THE COMPANY WAS FORMED FOR THE PRINCIPAL BUSINESS OF COMPUTER PROGRAMMING ACTIVITIES, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT, NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING, LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL INFERENCE APIS, AND RELATED TECHNOLOGY CONSULTING SERVICES; WHEREAS THE SHAREHOLDERS HAVE LAWFULLY SUBSCRIBED FOR THE ENTIRE REGISTERED CAPITAL AND HAVE APPOINTED THE UNDERSIGNED DIRECTORS, SUPERVISOR, AND SENIOR OFFICERS; NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. THE ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION AND ALL ANCILLARY INCORPORATION DOCUMENTS SUBMITTED TO THE MARKET SUPERVISION AUTHORITY ARE RATIFIED AND APPROVED IN THEIR ENTIRETY. 2. THE REGISTERED CAPITAL OF THE COMPANY IS SET AT RENMINBI TEN MILLION YUAN (RMB 10,000,000), DIVIDED INTO EQUITY INTERESTS AS FOLLOWS: SHAREHOLDER A SUBSCRIBES FOR SEVEN MILLION YUAN AND SHAREHOLDER B SUBSCRIBES FOR THREE MILLION YUAN. EACH SHAREHOLDER SHALL CONTRIBUTE CASH IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION SCHEDULE APPENDED TO THE ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION, AND ALL SUBSCRIBED CAPITAL SHALL BE FULLY PAID WITHIN FIVE YEARS FROM THE DATE OF INCORPORATION OR SUCH SHORTER PERIOD AS MAY BE REQUIRED BY LAW. 3. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation negative-list screening and company name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration through the Enterprise Registration One-Window Online Service Platform, with integrated consultation against the Foreign Investment Negative List managed by the Ministry of Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before submitting the formal incorporation file, the formation counsel must confirm that the proposed business scope, namely computer programming, artificial intelligence software development, LLM API provision, and related consulting services, does not appear on the Foreign Investment Negative List or does so only under a permitted non-restricted category. The proposed English and Chinese company names must be screened against the national enterprise name database to avoid conflict with protected names, trademarks, or public-interest restrictions. Counsel must prepare a name reservation application and submit it electronically. If the beneficial shareholder is a non-resident corporate entity, its certificate of incorporation and board resolutions must be notarized and apostilled under the Hague Apostille Convention, translated into Chinese, and submitted as part of the identity package.
required_dossiers: Company name reservation application
Proposed English and Chinese company names
Passport or certificate of incorporation of each shareholder
Notarized and apostilled corporate shareholder documents and board resolution
Power of attorney for the legalization agent
Proposed business scope matching ISIC 6201
Contact address and proposed registered address
Anti-money-laundering and beneficial ownership declaration where requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the electronic filing is queried due to name similarity, counsel must respond within ten working days by proposing two to three alternative names and resubmitting the name reservation through the same platform. If the business scope touches a restricted value-added telecommunications activity, counsel should narrow the scope to pure software and API technology services or apply for a specialized foreign-investment qualification before continuing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of WFOE establishment registration and issuance of the Unified Social Credit Code Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration; registration is accepted electronically through the Enterprise Registration One-Window Online Service Platform and completed in person at the relevant administrative service hall when physical signatures or identity verification are required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name pre-approval, counsel must assemble the complete incorporation dossier and submit the Company Establishment Registration Filing Application Form, the signed Articles of Association, the capital contribution schedule, and the identity documents of all directors, the supervisor, the legal representative, and the general manager. The registered address must be verified through a lease contract and a certificate of ownership or a landlord authorization letter. Foreign investors must submit apostilled corporate or personal identity documents with certified Chinese translations. On approval, the local Market Supervision Administration issues the Business License bearing a Unified Social Credit Code, which simultaneously completes tax registration, statistics registration, social insurance registration, and the foreign investment information report through the integrated multi-license system.
required_dossiers: Company Establishment Registration Filing Application Form
Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Capital contribution schedule
Company Name Pre-Approval Notice
Proof of registered address (lease, property ownership certificate, landlord authorization)
Passports or corporate identity documents of all shareholders
Notarized and apostilled foreign shareholder documents with Chinese translation
Appointment documents and identity cards for directors, supervisor, legal representative and general manager
Power of attorney and agent identity card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Market Supervision Administration returns a correction notice, counsel must rectify the defective items and resubmit within fifteen working days. If the rejection relates to the business scope, the scope must be redrafted to mirror the exact ISIC 6201 language and resubmitted without requesting restricted telecom or content-generation phraseology. If the identity verification of the foreign shareholder fails, new bank-approved notarization and apostille packages must be obtained and resubmitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation foreign investment information reporting, SAFE foreign exchange registration, and capital account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange acting through an authorized domestic bank; the integrated foreign investment information report is transmitted automatically to the Ministry of Commerce through the Market Supervision Administration's online filing system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Business License, the legal representative and the chief financial officer must finalize the foreign investment information report, open a basic deposit account and a foreign exchange capital account in RMB at the chosen SAFE-authorized bank, and complete the bank's SAFE foreign exchange registration for the WFOE. The authorized bank will verify the inward capital remittance against the registered capital amount and issue the relevant foreign exchange receipt verification documentation. If the shareholders prefer debt financing instead of equity injection, separate foreign debt registration under SAFE rules is required. All capital must remain in the capital account until the bank has completed the verification and permitted transfer to the general RMB working capital account. Formation counsel should also ensure that the board resolution authorizing bank signatories and spending limits is delivered to the bank in its original executed form.
required_dossiers: Original Business License
Articles of Association and all amendments
First Board Resolution on bank account opening and signatories
Company seal, financial seal, and legal representative seal
Legal representative passport or Chinese identity card
Passport and appointment letter of the Chief Financial Officer
SAFE foreign exchange registration forms supplied by the bank
Capital contribution schedule and board capital call resolutions
Power of attorney for any non-resident officer signing remotely
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or SAFE queries the capital remittance, counsel must provide a source-of-funds statement, board resolution, and audited or bank-stamped account statements. If the foreign exchange registration is returned due to a mismatch between the remitted amount and registered capital, the company must either correct the remittance or file an article amendment to adjust registered capital and resubmit. If the foreign investment information report is incomplete, the formation agent must file an amendment with the local Market Supervision Administration within the statutory filing window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax activation, payroll, social insurance, statistics, and office fire safety clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local taxation bureau of the State Taxation Administration, the Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, and the local Fire and Rescue Division for office occupancy fire safety.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Business License already creates the tax registration record, but the company must activate the tax account, appoint the tax officer and chief financial officer in the electronic tax portal, determine whether general VAT taxpayer status is beneficial, apply for invoice allocation, and complete payroll and social insurance registration with the human resources authorities. As this is an office-based digital service company, no environmental impact assessment or industrial discharge permit is required. The company must nevertheless secure the office premise through the local fire and rescue inspection, install fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, and evacuation signage, and retain a fire safety warden. All employment contracts, payroll records, and social insurance contributions should be registered in the national information systems to remain compliant with the Labor Contract Law and the Social Insurance Law.
required_dossiers: Unified Social Credit Code Business License
Legal representative identity document and appointment resolution
Lease contract and office floor plan
Fire safety installation checklist and maintenance records
Financial officer appointment and certified identification
Company seal and bank account confirmation
List of employees, employment contracts, and social insurance registration forms
Electronic tax portal activation forms and VAT status application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority issues a deviation notice, the financial officer must correct the general taxpayer application or invoicing settings and resubmit within ten working days. If social insurance registration is queried due to incomplete employee identification, the HR officer must upload corrected passports or identity cards. If the fire safety inspection identifies defects, the company must remedy all deficiencies within the period stated by the Fire and Rescue Division and request a re-inspection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Digital operational compliance filings for generative artificial intelligence, algorithms, internet information services, and data security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) for generative AI service filing and algorithm registration; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) for internet information service and ICP filing or license matters; Ministry of Public Security for networked system security filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: This ISIC 6201 platform is not subject to industrial or environmental licensing, but it must complete digital operational filings before publicly serving generative AI output in China. If the platform provides generative AI services to the public in mainland China, the company must submit a generative AI service filing and an internet information service algorithm registration to the CAC, accompanied by a safety self-assessment report, algorithm description, and technology measures for content identification. If the firm operates a public-facing website or app with commercial internet information services, an ICP filing or a value-added telecommunications license may be required under MIIT regulations, and the foreign-investment restrictions in the Negative List must be assessed. The company must also complete a multi-level protection scheme filing and security assessment with the public security authority for its information systems. If the platform serves only overseas customers and does not offer public services in mainland China, the company may treat these filings as not triggered, but cross-border data transfer rules under the Personal Information Protection Law and Data Security Law must still be analyzed.
required_dossiers: Business License and legal representative identity document
Generative AI service filing application with safety self-assessment
Algorithm registration and description for the large language model
AI service test account and log access for regulatory review
Data classification inventory and personal information protection policy
Website or API domain name and server hosting contract
ICP filing or value-added telecommunications license application, if applicable
Multi-level protection scheme security assessment report
Cross-border data transfer risk assessment and security filing, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CAC issues a rectification request, the company must suspend the affected feature, revise the algorithm or content moderation mechanism, and resubmit an amended safety assessment within ten working days. If MIIT challenges the ICP application, counsel should resubmit with a narrowed business scope or change the revenue model to infrastructure-as-a-service. If the public security filing fails the technical assessment, remediate all identified vulnerabilities and obtain a fresh testing report before re-filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. The target entity conducts ISIC 6201 computer programming and generative AI LLM API platform services; there is no physical manufacturing, chemical production, assembly, or warehousing activity, and therefore no industrial licensing board permit is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No manufacturing or operational plant license applies; the only relevant permissions are digital regulatory filings with the Cyberspace Administration of China and MIIT for internet information services and generative AI, as further described in the formation SOP.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable. The Ministry of Ecology and Environment and its local provincial ecology bureaus are not engaged because the activity is purely digital and office-based.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable and Exempt. ISIC 6201 does not create the physical industrial trigger for a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report, Environmental Registration, or Pollution Discharge Permit. No EIA tier is applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. There are no wastewater discharges, VOC emissions, hazardous chemical storage, or industrial solid waste streams. The company must only comply with ordinary office waste recycling, municipal water supply, and building sanitation rules applicable to commercial offices.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as a civil defense industrial permit. However, the WFOE office must obtain ordinary-occupancy fire safety clearance from the local Fire and Rescue Division before beginning operations, including fire extinguishers, evacuation signage, emergency lighting, and an annual fire safety inspection. Occupational health and safety duties under the Work Safety Law of the People's Republic of China apply to all office employees, and emergency response drills should be documented.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online electronic filing and registration via the China Electronic Taxpayer eTax portal (eTax/e-Chinatax) at the competent provincial-level STA access point for the WFOE registered address
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) The foreign parent incorporates a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) under Chinese Company Law through the local Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), obtaining a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) for tax purposes. 2) Within 30 calendar days after the business license is issued, the WFOE must complete tax registration through the STA eTax portal by submitting the business license, articles of association, legal representative identification, registered address proof, investor details and bank account information. 3) The STA issues a tax registration record and the WFOE is assigned the USCC-based taxpayer identification number, which is used for VAT, Corporate Income Tax, withholding and all other filings. 4) If projected annual taxable turnover will be at or above RMB 5,000,000, the entity must apply for VAT general taxpayer status to issue standard VAT invoices and claim input VAT credits. 5) If a foreign non-resident enterprise earns China-source income without a permanent establishment, it must complete non-resident enterprise tax registration via the withholding agent or directly through STA eTax to obtain a TIN and fulfil CIT and VAT withholding obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China does not operate a US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch pass-through election. The WFOE is mandatorily an entity-level Corporate Income Tax taxpayer resident in Mainland China. Available statutory elections include the VAT general taxpayer registration election, the small-scale taxpayer simplified-levy election when below the RMB 5,000,000 threshold, and software enterprise preferential tax treatment elections under the State Council software enterprise rules if the WFOE separately qualifies. No pass-through election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Tax registration and VAT registration are compulsory for every WFOE immediately upon issuance of the business license with no economic turnover threshold; the mandatory general (standard) VAT taxpayer registration threshold is RMB 5,000,000 of annual assessable taxable turnover, below which the small-scale taxpayer regime applies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices must be issued through the STA national fully digitalized electronic invoice platform (Electronic Invoice Service Platform), with real-time data transmission, API-based transaction reporting, unique digital invoice numbers and QR codes; no physical self-printing or manual tax stamping is permitted. The Golden Tax Phase IV system continuously matches invoice data against customs, treasury, exchange and enterprise bank records, and every zero-rated export invoice must be filed in the STA export tax refund declaration system with the supporting export documentation attached. Invoices issued outside the approved platform are invalid for input VAT deduction and export zero-rated refund purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Chinese VAT law, a WFOE may apply the 0% VAT zero-rating to exported software and information technology services, including AI/LLM API inference services, where: (i) the service is supplied to an overseas customer located outside Mainland China; (ii) the service is wholly consumed outside Mainland China with no onshore end-user or domestic use; (iii) the transaction is entered in the STA export tax refund system; and (iv) the export is documented by contract, commercial invoice, foreign exchange collection proof and service delivery evidence. Pure digital API services do not require physical customs export declarations; zero-rating is substantiated through service-export documentation and foreign exchange repatriation records, while any physical goods or media shipped as part of the export must additionally have a Customs Export Declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) for any physical goods or media exported in support of the AI API transaction
Bill of Lading or airway bill for physical exports
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / SAFE-recognized bank foreign-exchange settlement receipt evidencing collection of export proceeds from overseas
Signed cross-border service contract or purchase order identifying the AI/LLM API service, the non-resident purchaser, and the fee schedule
Commercial invoice issued through the STA e-invoice platform at the 0% VAT rate
Service delivery and consumption evidence such as API token usage logs, server access records or third-party platform statements proving offshore consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: STA, customs and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange jointly audit export zero-rating files. If supporting documentation is missing, internally inconsistent or fraudulent, the zero-rating or export refund is denied, the output VAT is clawed back, late payment surcharge accrues, and administrative penalties of 50% to 500% of the evaded or refunded tax are imposed under the Tax Administration and Collection Law. Cases involving forged FIRCs, false Customs declarations or fictitious export contracts may constitute fraudulent export tax refund crimes under the Criminal Law, carrying criminal fines and imprisonment up to life imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange-rate system with strict separation between current-account and capital-account convertibility. Under the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations, SAFE and PBoC jointly supervise RMB convertibility. Genuine current-account transactions of a WFOE engaged in AI API and software-export services, including token usage fees, subscription revenue, and SaaS/API royalties from overseas clients, are generally convertible once the transaction is supported by a signed economic contract, invoice, and payment record. Capital-account items, however, require case-by-case registration: FDI equity injections must be recorded through the FDI Business Registration system; the foreign exchange capital settlement account can convert the injected foreign currency into RMB, but disbursements from that account are subject to the 'four-by-four' deployment review and the negative-list use restrictions. Profit remittance to the foreign parent requires audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, mandatory statutory reserve contributions, and an SAFE outbound remittance declaration. Dividend repatriation is lawful only when retained earnings exist after corporate income tax and reserve requirements are satisfied. The authorities encourage RMB settlement but USD is still accepted for bona fide trade and service receipts. In practice, the WFOE must avoid any mismatch between the declared purpose code and the actual underlying business, maintain a documented trail from issuance contract to token consumption, and ensure that any cryptocurrency/USDC payment is converted offshore and never introduced into the onshore banking perimeter as a direct settlement token. Accordingly, the treasury blueprint should maintain separate onshore CNY operating liquidity and offshore USD receipts, with each cross-border flow anchored to a verifiable commercial event.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds, including AI API fees from overseas customers, must be repatriated to China through a designated foreign exchange bank and reported to SAFE. The statutory requirement is repatriation and verification, not a fixed mandatory surrender percentage; after the 2012 SAFE reforms the WFOE may retain foreign exchange or settle it to CNY based on its treasury need. For goods exports the standard collection period is 90 days after customs declaration; for services the collection period should follow the contract and, in practice, be completed within 180 days from invoice maturity. Any delayed collection beyond the normal trade period requires a deferred-receipt registration or an application to the local SAFE branch. The mandatory conversion ratio is 0% because there is no fixed quota; however, the foreign exchange received must be either retained in a compliant current-account receipt account or settled through the bank on a transaction-specific basis, and any surplus not substantiated by the underlying export/service contract must be reversed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Settlement Account for FDI and Basic Operational Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (RMB) and Multi-currency Current Account
Capital Escrow Account for Registered Capital and Operational Settlement Account
Corporate Foreign Exchange Account and RMB Basic Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs have very low viability as the primary banking layer for an onshore Chinese WFOE. Non-bank payment institutions providing account, clearing, and payment services in China must obtain a PBoC Payment Business License; no foreign EMI holds that license. Therefore Revolut Business, Wise, Airwallex, and similar offshore digital entities cannot open onshore RMB bank accounts, issue a domestic settlement account, or produce the SAFE capital verification documentation. They may only be used as auxiliary offshore collection tools for the foreign parent receiving USD before making a regulated MT103 equity injection. All onshore treasury duties—FDI registration, capital verification, CNY settlement, trade payments, tax remittance, and documentary evidence—must sit with a licensed PRC commercial bank. Any attempt to route WFOE operating revenue through an offshore EMI to bypass SAFE will trigger an AML red flag and legal exposure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the WFOE legal representative during initial account opening in mainland China. Most PRC commercial banks require the legal representative to appear in-branch with original passport, the enterprise seal, the financial official seal, and the company license, and to complete a compliance interview and risk-assessment questionnaire. Foreign shareholders or directors may provide notarized and legalized powers of attorney, but the statutory legal representative must execute the account-opening documents on-site or, in a small number of bank branches, through a supervised remote video interview with prior branch approval. Remote consular proxy opening for the legal representative is not a legal right and is generally discouraged for a WFOE with non-resident ownership; banks may accept an authenticated board resolution appointing the on-site authorized signatory, yet the legal representative’s identity verification and AML interview still dominate the decision.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete FDI registration or capital-verification mismatch on the parent equity injection, causing the bank to suspect disguised capital inflow and violation of SAFE capital-account rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI Business Registration Form; written board resolution approving the capital contribution; foreign parent audited financial statements; bank-to-bank SWIFT confirmation showing purpose code for equity investment; certified PRC CPA capital verification report; payment source and beneficial ownership declaration; and a detailed narrative explaining the timing, currency, and use of the injected funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity created by a Hong Kong or offshore intermediate holding company sitting between the ultimate global parent and the mainland WFOE.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate and Certificate of Incorporation; complete shareholding register tracing to each natural person; notarized memorandum and articles of association; UBO declaration signed by each 25% or greater natural-person owner; apostilled or legalized corporate resolutions; intermediary bank reference letter; and an organizational-chain memo showing no shell-layer concealment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AI API platform revenue includes or is suspected to include USDC, cryptocurrency, or high-volume small-amount payments from unverified global developers, triggering virtual-currency and sanctions-screening concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A granular audit of the offshore payment gateway pipeline showing conversion of USDC into fiat before any WFOE bank receipt; endpoint-user transaction ledger with geolocation and IP data; customer onboarding KYC and sanctions/PEP screening evidence; independent legal opinion confirming that the WFOE does not operate a virtual-currency exchange or money-service business in mainland China; and a contractual representation from the parent that no onshore RMB settlement is connected to wallet addresses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Current-account remittance with ambiguous service code, e.g., 'technical services' or 'professional fees', without proof that AI API consumption actually occurred, creating a false trade or tax-evasion suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed API platform license and subscription agreements; itemized invoices with token-based usage measurement; server/API usage logs, authenticated daily or monthly consumption reports; tax filing records for zero-rated software export or VAT exemption; SAFE Foreign Exchange Survey declaration matching the exact purpose code; and third-party attestation from an independent auditor on the revenue recognition model.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign parent must execute the capital contribution through a regulated banking channel, using SWIFT MT103, with the remittance purpose code corresponding to equity investment in a foreign-invested enterprise. The funds must land in the WFOE's designated foreign-currency capital settlement account at a licensed PRC commercial bank. After receipt, the WFOE must complete the SAFE FDI registration or update, present the FDI Business Registration Form, and instruct the bank to settle the foreign currency into RMB. The bank will register the capital settlement in the SAFE foreign exchange platform, and a qualified PRC CPA must issue a capital verification report. Disbursements from the settled capital account must comply with the negative-list use restrictions and be supported by invoices, contracts, and payroll/tax documents. No personal wallet, offshore EMI, or third-party collection account may be used as the inbound route for registered capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For AI API service disbursements to overseas cloud providers, model vendors, license holders, and independent contractors, the standard clearing rail is a current-account SWIFT MT103 remittance supported by a service agreement, invoice, payment schedule, and SAFE purpose code. For any physical-goods import incidental to the WFOE operations, a commercial letter of credit (MT700) or documentary collection is permissible, but the bank will require transport documents, customs declarations, and matching invoices. The WFOE must not use personal cards or crypto rails for corporate trade settlements; all outbound payments require the corporate seal, the mandated bank reviewer sign-off, and proof of tax withholding if the payment includes royalty or service-royalty components.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward contracts (CNY/USD) for genuine current-account exposure are permissible, with SAFE real-demand confirmation through a designated PRC bank and no speculative gapping.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps are permitted only for hedging confirmed offshore liabilities or FX debt positions, require the bank’s internal product eligibility and SAFE filing, and must be matched to an existing notional.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not lawful for the onshore WFOE treasury; only the offshore parent may execute NDFs as a hedge, and those contracts cannot settle against the WFOE’s onshore account.
FX option collars and risk reversals are permitted for hedging real trade or service exposure, but each transaction must be supported by an underlying contract, invoice, and SAFE documentary check.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Report (annual return) under the Interim Regulations on Enterprise Information Publicity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via local Market Supervision Bureau and the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 of each calendar year for the preceding fiscal year; no extension or anniversary-based alternative
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If not filed by June 30, the WFOE is placed on the abnormal operations list (enterprise credit exception list). The listing is published publicly and remains until the overdue report is filed; removal may be applied for within 10 working days after filing. If the entity remains on that list for more than 3 consecutive years, SAMR moves it to the serious illegal and dishonest enterprise list, subjecting the legal representative to restrictions on travel, credit accommodation, government procurement, bidding, and equity registration. False or fraudulent annual report content is sanctioned under SAMR and MOFCOM rules with fines of RMB 10,000 to 300,000 (approximately USD 1,400 to 42,000). No annual renewal fee is payable to the government.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Information Report for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM); data collected through the SAMR integrated National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 of each calendar year, concurrent with the SAMR annual enterprise information report; no separate annual declaration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures, a WFOE that fails to report, or reports falsified information, is ordered by the local commerce department to correct the omission within a time limit. If the correction is not made, a fine of RMB 10,000 to 300,000 (approximately USD 1,400 to 42,000) may be imposed. The enterprise may also be recorded in the abnormal credit publicity list, impairing receipt of foreign-investment preferential treatment, foreign-exchange verification, tax benefits, and subsequent registration changes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Settlement and Payment (annual CIT return and final tax payment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) / competent local tax authority through the electronic tax filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By May 31 of the year following each calendar year (financial year-end December 31); quarterly prepayments remain due during the year but are settled in this annual filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing itself triggers an administrative penalty of up to RMB 2,000 per form, or RMB 2,000 to 10,000 for a serious refusal to file. Late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax for each overdue day, equivalent to approximately 18.25% per annum. Underpayment caused by concealment or false bookkeeping is subject to a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax; where criminal tax evasion is established, the responsible legal representative and finance officer are liable to prosecution. The tax authority may also freeze bank accounts, restrain invoicing, and seize assets to secure the overdue tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual maintenance proof of statutory registers and beneficial-ownership declaration (register audit reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the annual report portal; internal register audit at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate filing deadline; the register audit must be completed no later than April 30 each year so that the annual enterprise information report and foreign investment report (January to June) reflect the true position as of December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Shareholding transfers, director changes, registered capital changes, and actual controller/beneficial-owner changes must be filed with SAMR within 30 days of the change. A failure to keep registers in order or to file a timely change is subject to SAMR correction orders; persistent non-compliance can lead to the abnormal operations list, rejection of notarized share transfer approvals, and fines of RMB 10,000 to 100,000 for registration violations under the Market Entity Registration Regulations. The register audit does not exempt the WFOE from the annual report deadline.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: There are no quantitative balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount thresholds that exempt a China WFOE from the statutory audit. Article 164 of the PRC Company Law and the PRC Accounting Law require every company, including a WFOE LLC, to prepare annual financial statements and have them audited by an independent certified public accounting firm licensed in China. The Foreign Investment Law and the Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures further require the WFOE to maintain audited financial statements as the basis for the annual foreign-investment report. If the enterprise qualifies under the Ministry of Finance Small Enterprise Accounting Standard, simplified accounting may be used, but the audit obligation remains. For an AI/LLM API platform with revenue from Stripe and USDC, the audit must independently test revenue recognition from API token usage, digital-asset receipts, foreign-exchange conversion, VAT treatment, and intercompany transactions; the auditor must be a Chinese CPA firm with no disqualifying relationship. The absence of balance-sheet or headcount safe harbor means a dormant WFOE is still required to incur the audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (Chinese GAAP/CAS), supplemented by the Ministry of Finance Small Enterprise Accounting Standard where eligible. IFRS may be used for consolidated foreign-parent reporting but cannot replace the PRC statutory audit framework. The annual CIT return is computed on PRC tax bases with adjustments from CAS financial statements. If the WFOE is the subsidiary of a foreign listed group, the Chinese CPA may also issue a separate IFRS-comfort or agreed-upon-procedures report, but the statutory audit opinion must address CAS/Chinese GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must identify its beneficial owner(s) as any natural person ultimately owning or controlling the entity (commonly assessed at 25% shareholding or effective control); this information must be recorded and reported to SAMR as part of the annual enterprise information report, and to MOFCOM as part of the foreign-investment annual report. Any change in shareholding, ultimate beneficial owner, actual controller, or registered capital must be submitted to SAMR as a registration change within 30 days. The annual report window from January 1 to June 30 serves as the annual confirmation fixing the beneficial-ownership picture at December 31; if the current data differs from the last filed register, the enterprise must first file a change registration under the 30-day rule and then confirm the updated position in the annual report.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600–1,800 per year for a licensed agent/registered office address in a Tier-1 Chinese city; no separate government fee for maintaining the registered address
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–6,000 for a small AI/LLM API WFOE with simple capital structure; USD 6,000–15,000 for cross-border payment, USDC treasury, or parent-consolidation complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Applicable preferential rates and incentives for a PRC WFOE operating an AI LLM API platform include: (i) New High-and-New-Technology Enterprises (HNTE) pay 15% CIT; (ii) small-and-low-profit enterprises within the statutory thresholds pay an effective 5% CIT; (iii) qualifying Key Software Enterprises may pay 10%; (iv) encouraged industries in the Western Region or Hainan Free Trade Port may be eligible for 15%; (v) the R&D expense super-deduction allows an additional 100% deduction for qualifying R&D expenditures; (vi) technology-transfer income up to RMB 5 million is exempt and the excess may be taxed at 50%; (vii) software enterprises may access the two-year exemption plus half-rate period under the software enterprise preferential policy if the AI/LLM platform qualifies as software development and related services. All incentives are subject to genuine substance, revenue composition, headcount and R&D ratio tests in China Mainland; shell arrangements will be denied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, A-Type), together with the Basic Information Sheet A000000, adjustment schedules A105000/A105050/A105080, loss carryforward schedule A106000, preferential schedules A107010/A107012/A107014, foreign tax credit schedule A108010/A108000, and the Annual Related-Party Transactions Reporting Table (G101000/G102000/G103000), all e-filed through the State Taxation Administration's Electronic Tax Portal (Electronic Tax Bureau).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual reconciliation return plus quarterly provisional CIT filings during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed within five months after the fiscal year end; for a calendar-year WFOE the statutory deadline is May 31 of the following year. Quarterly provisional payments are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter. Non-resident dividend withholding and withholding returns are due on the earlier of the payment date or remittance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer details: Unified Social Credit Code, legal English name, WFOE status, jurisdiction, statutory business scope (ISIC 6201, NAICS 541511), number of employees, registered capital, tax-resident status, and contact information of the legal representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the WFOE as a Chinese tax-resident enterprise taxed on worldwide income. The box must not conflate the foreign shareholder's status; the non-resident shareholder's tax filing is a separate withholding-layer event. Ensure the e-filing account reflects the WFOE as a limited liability company with non-resident ownership allowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 (Main Table A100000 Lines 1-3: Revenue, Cost and Taxes)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting operating revenue generated from LLM inference API tokens, subscription fees, usage metering and derived data products; matching operating cost for cloud infrastructure, GPU/TPU amortization, licensing fees, and business taxes and surcharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where API revenue is derived from servers located in mainland China, the source is generally domestic; maintain server logs and billing metering to substantiate the source allocation. If the WFOE resells foreign cloud capacity to Chinese customers, avoid double-counting and confirm whether a permanent establishment of the foreign vendor is created in China, triggering tax registration and withholding obligations on fees paid to the foreign cloud provider.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 (Main Table A100000 Lines 4-6: Selling, Administrative and Finance Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses, general and administrative expenses, finance costs, salaries, cloud bandwidth, consulting fees, marketing expenses, and interest on intercompany or third-party debt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign affiliates for management fees, marketing, technical services, or brand licensing must pass the arm's-length test and must not constitute double-dipping cost allocations. The tax authority will disallow a deduction unless the foreign affiliate provides true services, has substantive personnel and assets abroad, and the WFOE documents the benefit received. Any amount that economically represents a dividend or capital contribution will be recharacterised as a non-deductible distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 (Main Table A100000 Line 7: Accounting Profit and Taxable Income Reconciliations)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax, adjusted via Schedule A105000 for permanent and temporary differences, tax-exempt income, non-deductible expenses, R&D super-deductions, and deemed profit remittance adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border payments, do not deduct the WFOE's income tax withholding paid on behalf of the foreign beneficiary unless the contract places the tax burden on the WFOE under a gross-up regime and the tax is otherwise statutorily dediductible; in practice such grossed-up WHT is often treated as a non-deductible foreign tax. Prepare a reconciliation explaining every tax treaty rate claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of prior-year losses, current-year taxable income, and losses available to carry forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Chinese tax-resident WFOE's own losses may be applied against its own future taxable income; losses cannot be surrendered to or received from foreign group affiliates. For standard companies the carryforward is five years; HNTE businesses may carry forward ten years for qualifying losses. A foreign acquiring company cannot step up tax basis through a merger or acquisition unless a formal tax special reorganisation filing is made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 (Schedules A107010/A107012/A107014: Tax Incentives and Preferential Rates)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims for the 15% HNTE rate, 15% encouraged-industry Western Region rate, small-and-low-profit preferential effective 5% rate, R&D super-deduction, software enterprise holiday, and Hainan Free Trade Port 15% regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To claim the HNTE 15% rate, the WFOE must prove statutory R&D intensity, high-tech revenue ratio, qualified R&D personnel ratio, IP ownership and core technology relevance to LLM inference APIs. The tax authority will investigate whether the Chinese entity is the true economic owner and developer of the AI software and algorithms; if the IP is held by an offshore parent with a bare licence back to the WFOE, the HNTE claim will fail.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit claimed for income taxes paid abroad on foreign-source income, including overseas API licensing, foreign withholding taxes, or taxes on digital service revenues.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign tax credit is limited to the Chinese tax payable on the same foreign-source income before the credit. Credits are not available if the foreign income was routed through a shell company in a zero-tax or low-tax jurisdiction without commercial purpose. Preserve foreign tax assessments and the full chain of ownership and payment evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 (Annual Related-Party Transactions Reporting Table G102000/G103000 and Transfer Pricing Documentation Statement)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Segmented disclosure of controlled transactions: sale of API tokens and model licences to offshore affiliates, purchase of GPU cloud capacity, royalty payments for algorithms and LLM training data, intercompany loans, cost-sharing arrangements, and management or technical services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the counterparty tax jurisdiction, transaction type, amount, the functional profile (functions, assets, risks), the transfer pricing method selected, and the arm's-length range or margin achieved. A missing, incomplete, or false related-party schedule is a standalone compliance infraction and will cause the WFOE to lose contemporaneous documentation protection during audit, exposing it to recharacterisation under China's special tax adjustment regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law (TCAL) Articles 32 and 62, late filing triggers a fine of up to RMB 2,000 in ordinary cases and up to RMB 10,000 in serious cases, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax. If the late filing is accompanied by deliberate underreporting or fraudulent tax avoidance, TCAL Article 63 imposes a penalty equal to 50% to 500% of the evaded tax and criminal liability under PRC Criminal Law Article 201 when the tax evaded is relatively large and exceeds 10% of the tax payable; penalties and imprisonment can escalate if the amount is above RMB 200,000 and exceeds 30% of the tax payable.
